topics.title: How does the internet work?
topics.angle: Your cat video just travelled through an undersea cable in under a second.
topics.chorusIdea: Packets on the move, hop hop hop!

topics.title: What do mitochondria actually do?
topics.angle: Every cell in your body has its own tiny power plant.

topics.title: What is a black hole?
topics.angle: What if you squeezed the whole Earth down to the size of a marble?
topics.chorusIdea: Too much stuff in too little space!

topics.title: Why is the sky blue?
topics.angle: Sunlight is every colour at once, so why do we only see blue?

topics.title: How do vaccines work?
topics.angle: Your immune system can practise for a fight before it happens.
topics.chorusIdea: Train it, remember it, beat it!

topics.title: How do plants make food from sunlight?
topics.angle: A tree is mostly built out of air.
topics.chorusIdea: Light, water, air: make it sweet!

topics.title: What is electricity?
topics.angle: The electrons in your wires barely move, so how does the light turn on instantly?
topics.chorusIdea: Push, push, pass it down the line!

topics.title: How does GPS know where you are?
topics.angle: Your phone finds you by listening to clocks in space.
topics.chorusIdea: Three, four satellites, here I am!

topics.title: Can an AI agent go rogue?
topics.angle: An AI that can click, browse, and use tools can do more than answer a question—so what happens when it makes the wrong move?
topics.chorusIdea: One more click, one more call—who's in control of it all?

topics.title: Why does AI use so much electricity?
topics.angle: Every AI answer has a physical cost: chips switching billions of times, plus the cooling needed to keep data centres alive.
topics.chorusIdea: Compute, cool, repeat the beat—where the watts meet the heat!

topics.title: How can an atomic clock measure time so precisely?
topics.angle: The most precise clocks don't count gears or pendulums—they count the incredibly steady rhythm of atoms.
topics.chorusIdea: Tick by tick, atom beat—time so fine you can't compete!

topics.title: Why does Mars grow a giant cloud every day?
topics.angle: A cloud stretching hundreds of miles appears on Mars again and again—what makes a planet's atmosphere do that?
topics.chorusIdea: Rise and stretch across the red—Mars makes clouds above its head!

topics.title: How can a robot dog run a marathon on one battery?
topics.angle: A robot running for hours is a puzzle in energy, balance, motors, and heat—not just a clever set of legs.
topics.chorusIdea: Balance, motors, battery flow—how far can a robot go?

topics.title: Why are giant batteries becoming a better deal than gas turbines?
topics.angle: The AI boom is changing how power gets stored and delivered—why can a giant battery sometimes beat a power plant on cost?
topics.chorusIdea: Store the spark, release the power—save it up for peak demand hour!
